Main.sentence: West Pullman is a neighborhood located on the far south side of the ___E:city of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_Chicago)___ , ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ .
It is one of the 77 ___E:official community areas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago)___ of Chicago.

The neighborhood was initially inhabited by workers of the ___E:Pullman Train Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman_Company)___ looking to escape the grip of ___E:the company town U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman,_Chicago)___ , but soon swelled with industrial workers of all stripes.
The commercial corridor of Kensington/115th Street was one of many Italian communities within Chicago, and now hosts a Hispanic enclave.

It is bounded on the north by 115th Street, on the east by the former ___E:Illinois Central Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Central_Railroad)___ , on the south by the ___E:Calumet River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_River)___ and ___E:Riverdale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverdale,_Chicago)___ , on the west by ___E:Calumet Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calumet_Park,_Illinois)___ , ___E:Blue Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Island)___ and Ashland Avenue.

According to a June 2017 analysis by the ___E:Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Metropolitan_Agency_for_Planning)___ , there were 27,982 people and 9,058 households in West Pullman.
From 2000 to 2015, the area lost more than 20% of its residents.

The ___E:racial makeup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_and_ethnicity_in_the_United_States_Census#2010_census)___ of the area was 1% White, 93.39% African American, 0.24% Asian, 0.54% from other races.
Residents who identify as Hispanic or Latino of any race were 4.83% of the population.
The age distribution was 29.7% under the age of 19, 19.3% from 20 to 34, 17.7% from 35 to 49, 18.5% from 50 to 64, and 14.8% 65 or older.
The median age was 35 years.
The median income is $33,898.

After the expulsion of the ___E:Potawatomi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi)___ as part of the ___E:1833 Treaty of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1833_Treaty_of_Chicago)___ , the area that is now West Pullman was settled by ___E:westbound settlers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_pioneer)___ .
In the 1880s, real estate speculators created the West Pullman Land Association to develop land between Wentworth and Ashland Avenues.

The Association was successful in industrial development, and later residential development before the ___E:Panic of 1893 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_of_1893)___ , the ___E:Pullman Strike of 1894 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman_Strike)___ dealt an economic blow that resulted in bankruptcy.
Like many of Chicago's community areas, West Pullman consists of multiple smaller communities.
The oldest of these was ___E:Kensington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington,_Chicago)___ , founded in 1852 at the junction of the Illinois Central and Michigan Central railroads.

Nicknamed "Bumtown", the commercial district around Kensington station was frequented by residents of neighboring Pullman, a dry town. The second of these communities was the village of Gano. The area of Gano was populated by Pullman workers who desired to own their own homes and escape from the corporate control of George Pullman's company town. Many ethnic groups called the area home, including Italians, Poles, Hungarians, Lithuanians, Ukrainians, Armenians, many of whom built houses of worship and cultural centers, like ___E:St. Michael Ukrainian Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Michael_Eastern_Catholic_Church,_West_Pullman)___ .

The Pullman Company shut down in 1968, dealing a major blow to the entire area. Further deindustrialization, combined with suburban development, led to a similar racial turnover in West Pullman as occurred in much of the South Side; the neighborhood was 99.8% white in 1960 and 94% black in 1980.
Located along several major railways and the Calumet Sag Channel, West Pullman was and remains a mostly blue collar community.
Much of the heavy industry the area relied on disappeared in the late 20th century, and it lags behind the rest of Chicago economically.
West Pullman has an unemployment rate of 19.9%, compared to a city-wide rate of 8.4%.
Habitat for Humanity has built and is continuing to build homes in the community.
West Pullman has worked to clean up and rehabilitate old industrial sites.
With the help of the EPA, community organizers managed to turn a brownfield into a community garden.
West Pullman is also home to the largest urban ___E:photovoltaic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photovoltaic)___ solar plant in the United States.

The 10 MW plant utilizes 32,800 ___E:SunPower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SunPower)___ solar panels, spans 39 acres (160,000 m 2 ), and generates enough power to supply energy to approximately 1500 homes in the Midwest.
It is owned and operated by ___E:Exelon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exelon)___ and came online in early 2010.

According to the ___E:Pritzker School of Medicine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritzker_School_of_Medicine)___ , fourteen percent (14%) of the West Pullman population is uninsured, though ninety-two percent (92%) report having a consistent primary care provider.
The obesity rate is fifty-three percent (53%).
West Pullman is a stronghold of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ .

In the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2016)___ , West Pullman cast 12,473 votes for ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ and cast 217 votes ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .

It was Clinton's 11th largest margin of victory in the 76 community areas she won.  In the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2012)___ , West Pullman cast 14,496 votes for ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and 86 votes for ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ .
It was Obama's 8th largest margin of victory in the 76 community areas he won.

At the local level, West Pullman is located in Chicago's 9th and 34th wards represented by Democrats ___E:Anthony Beale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Beale)___ and ___E:Carrie Austin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Austin)___ respectively.

West Pullman is home to four stations on the ___E:Metra Electric District's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ Blue Island branch; ___E:Racine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racine_Avenue_station)___ , ___E:State Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Street_station_(Illinois))___ , ___E:Stewart Ridge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_Ridge_station)___ , and ___E:West Pullman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pullman_station)___ .

Main line Electric District trains stop at ___E:Kensington station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kensington/115th_Street_station)___ , just across the community's northern boundary.  ___E:Red Ahead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Ahead)___ , a program to extend the Red Line south to 130th Street, would result in a new station at Michigan Avenue in West Pullman.
In 2025, it was estimated that this project would begin construction in 2026 and will be completed in 2030.
Habitat For Humanity is interjecting single-family homes throughout the neighborhood for improvement.
Cottage Grove Ave is being extended Southbound from E 115th St. to E 130th St. with light and visual improvements.
E 115th St. and S. Cottage Grove Ave will see train station improvements along with retail improvements.
